per_source.finding: Maren Dovell’s 12 June note to adviser Kit Wenslow is a credible agenda and records-handling instruction. The 15:50 secure transmission precedes the 16:00 BST cut-off. One 17 June slot with separate working papers and minute entries fits the stated trustee appointments. The appointments book is cited, not enclosed. The note neither records a distribution decision nor authorises payment.

Tess Arnay’s 9 June certified extract to the adviser is a plausible selective copy of the 21 October 2022 Alder Quay deed lodged as PD-6834-R. The disclosed schedule omission is consistent with the extract’s purpose. Clauses 3, 4 and 6 distinguish original objects, payment appointments and later additions. Identification by a jointly stated parent reference is unusually specific but credible as an express deed term for shared custody, not a general rule.

Bram Lerrit’s 9 June certification to the adviser identifies the separately lodged Flint Orchard deed, PD-6894-R, and discloses that schedules were not reproduced. The format and phrasing are distinct from Alder Quay’s while covering comparable business. Clauses 2, 5 and 8 distinguish eligibility, direct application for an object’s benefit and addition by joint delivery. The register’s evidential role does not give the custodian a trustee power.

Alys Morcant’s same-day transcript for the trustees’ records desk, forwarded on 10 June, is credible as a record made before the original left the signing room. It reproduces both deed signatures and separate attestations by one witness present in person. The reference SD-Q7M2 identifies the instrument, not its parent. The transcript is neither another counterpart nor evidence of delivery, and the instrument adds an object only; it makes no payment appointment.

Gideon Sarn’s 11 June certified extract went to the trust office for onward supply to the adviser. It records both trustees confirming PD-6894-R against SD-Q7M2 and releasing one signed original for immediate delivery at 11:30 GMT on 26 March, not in escrow. This establishes the Flint Orchard link on the supplied record. The explanation ruling out title searches and counterpart numbering is unusually explicit, but credible in a certified extract explaining shared-custody conventions. The vault original was not forwarded.

Ione Berrick’s personal letter to both trustees has a credible postal, scanning and forwarding path; intake supplies the year omitted from the heading. The stale estimate and practical help with paperwork are ordinary operational details. Permission to pass on an estimate is not payment authority. Ione’s wish for Sella Quist to be considered in her own right is not a designation or a request to redirect, deduct from or set up payments.

Una Cresset’s 11 June reconciliation for the records desk and pack compiler credibly distinguishes the £12.60 postage reimbursement through the office operating account from the unpaid, unauthorised £8.40 print-shop query. The postage slip was attached to the underlying claim, not stated to accompany this copy. Neither item was recharged. Sella’s payee and queries-contact entry is confined to EX-K4; it is not a settlement payment instruction.

limitations: The cut-off file supports Ione Berrick and Emmett Vann for Alder Quay, and Ione Berrick, Orla Penrick and Rhea Marden for Flint Orchard. Rhea was added to Flint Orchard on joint delivery on 26 March. No removal or addition of Sella is evidenced. The adviser has certified extracts and a transcript, not the full deeds, supplemental original or appointments book.

No distribution authorisation for either settlement is evidenced in the pack. That is not proof that the underlying decision and payment registers contain no entries. Reconcile each settlement separately before deciding or paying, and keep any later papers outside the closed preparation set.
